newsitem.title: POLAND: Espebepe to offer creditors new debt deal.
newsitem.headline: Espebepe to offer creditors new debt deal.

text.p: Debt-ridden Polish construction firm Espebepe SA wants to offer its creditors a new programme to save the company from bankruptcy which includes raising the firm's share capital, Espebepe's president said.

Andrzej Hass told Reuters on Tuesday the company, which has debts of about 75 million zlotys, had already presented to shareholders the new programme which includes a 20-percent raise of share capital, but declined to give any details.
"We have already presented the programme (of raising share capital) to our shareholders and they accepted it," Hass said. @

Espepebe earlier offered its creditors a debt restructuring deal envisaging a 95-percent debt write-off, but creditors' meetings on March 14 and April 14 failed to reach any decisions and a new one was set for May 16.
If the plan failed, Espebepe could become the first bankruptcy on the Warsaw Stock Exchange since it was restored in 1991.
It was not immediately clear whether the new Espebepe proposal would envisage a share or convertible bond issue, as proposed earlier by its largest creditor Pomorski Bank Kredytowy SA (PBKS).
PBKS earlier insisted that the debt restructuring be combined with a debt-for-equity swap through a convertible bond issue, but Espebepe rejected it as too time-consuming.

Espebepe said in a statement that during Monday's creditors meeting a large majority of creditors' votes was in favour of the debt write-off deal, but it still lacked a required majority of capital represented in the debts.
